title: Sequence-Length Clustering & Kernel Ensemble Scheduler (online micro-benchmark tuner)
creator: Marco Rivera
description: Problem: kernel choice in the runtime currently uses a static heuristic tuned for average sequence lengths and hardware generation, which leaves tail latency and cost on the table for workloads with multimodal sequence-length distributions (chat vs summarization vs embed). This ticket proposes a lightweight online kernel-ensemble scheduler that clusters incoming requests by sequence-length distribution and runtime signature, then selects a small ensemble of pre-profiled kernels per cluster using an online micro-benchmarking signal and a cost-accuracy tradeoff model.
proposal_summary: 1) Offline: aggregate per-customer request seq-len histograms and run targeted micro-profiling on candidate kernels across representative seq-len buckets. 2) Runtime: classify requests into clusters (short/medium/long + kv-prefill vs decode-heavy) and consult a tiny ensemble (2-3 kernels) with a fast cost model. 3) Online adapt: periodically run 50-200 token micro-benchmarks under low-priority lanes to validate and update kernel scores; switch only when predicted win > threshold to avoid oscillation. 4) Prefill/decode scheduling: bias prefill-heavy requests to kernels with fast KV-cache prefetching and memory-friendly attention paths; schedule decode-heavy requests to kernels optimized for compute per token. Includes safe fallbacks and conservative rate-limited switching.
risks_and_tradeoffs:
- Micro-benchmark noise can cause harmful oscillation if switches are too aggressive. Mitigation: exponential smoothing of scores and hysteresis guardrails.
- Extra scheduling logic increases scheduler complexity and potential bug surface; mitigation: keep classifier simple (histogram bucketing + 3 features) and feature-flag rollout.
- Storage for per-customer profiles increases metadata; mitigation: compact histograms and TTLs (30d).
success_metrics: P95 latency reduction for multi-modal workloads >= 10% (measured per-route)
Unit token cost reduction >= 5% on average for mixed workloads
No increase in error-rate or correctness regressions after kernel switches
Fallback and safety: <= 1% additional retries or fallbacks triggered
acceptance_criteria: Design doc accepted by runtime/infra leads (link in attachments)
Proof-of-concept shows stable wins on 3 representative workloads (chat, summarization, embeddings)
Feature-flagged rollout with canary on 5% of traffic and dashboarded metrics
Automated tests for classifier and hysteresis logic in runtime test-suite
work_items: Offline profiler pipeline: add seq-len bucketing and micro-benchmark runner
Runtime classifier: implement histogram bucketing + feature extraction
Kernel ensemble store: compact per-cluster kernel scores with TTL
Online micro-benchmark job: low-priority background lane + smoothing logic
Prefill vs decode routing policy: expose config knobs and defaults
comments: 2026-02-15 Marco Rivera: Initial write-up and perf hypothesis. Attached high-level design doc. Asked infra for profiling quota.

2026-02-22 Aisha Patel: Spike completed—offline profiler shows that 3 kernels cover > 95% of cases per-cluster for our internal workloads. Baseline graphs uploaded to Grafana. PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3829 (WIP).
2026-02-28 SRE review (I. Chen): Concern about metadata growth. Agreed on 30d TTL and compact histograms. Added as constraint in proposal.

2026-03-03 Quentin Lee (Perf): Micro-benchmark noise observed at low QPS; recommended increasing sample size and smoothing window. We updated tuning to require at least 200 tokens sampled before switch is allowed.

2026-03-07 Aisha Patel: Implemented classifier and ensemble store. Unit tests added. Running canary in internal staging against synthetic spike traces. See dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/seqlen/ensemble-tuner-staging

2026-03-10 Marco Rivera: Decided on conservative rollout: start with 1% traffic canary for 1 week, then 5% for 2 weeks if steady. Open follow-ups: autoscale interaction testing and canary rollback automation (ENG-42788).
